📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AirPods Pro 3 (now only $149, down from $249) offer many advantages over AirPods Pro 2, but after a year of use, the improvements to Active Noise Cancellation alone have proven worth the upgrade.

I’ve been using AirPods Pro 3 for over a year, and they had a lot to live up to because I already loved AirPods Pro 2 so much. Initially I found the new ear tips less comfortable, but thankfully that issue went away after a little extra time.

Sources indicate that some highlights of AirPods Pro 3 include the longer battery life, with 8 hours per charge compared to 6 on the previous model. The charging case’s upcoming Ultra Wideband chip also makes it easier to find when it’s lost. Some users will appreciate the heart rate sensor, but I wear an Apple Watch all the time so it doesn’t benefit me much.

It has been revealed that these new features are nice to have, but Active Noise Cancellation is where AirPods Pro 3 become a major upgrade. Apple says it’s “the world’s best in-ear Active Noise Cancellation.” Here’s how the new ANC compares to previous models:.

Industry observers note that I spend nearly my entire workday with AirPods Pro 3 in my ears. Whether I’m working from home with young kids around or at a busy coffee shop, I rely on ANC to block out background noise and help me focus.

One reason I’ve been especially impressed with the ANC upgrades is that I didn’t have any real complaints about ANC on AirPods Pro 2. But Apple managed to deliver improvements in AirPods Pro 3 I had no idea I needed, and when I’ve tried going back to AirPods Pro 2 I couldn’t believe how much noise was let in.

If Active Noise Cancellation is notable to you, I highly recommend AirPods Pro 3.

#2194. 5 underrated Apple Watch shortcuts you can set up in minutes

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1534 w)

5 underrated Apple Watch shortcuts you can set up in minutes

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1534 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Your Apple Watch can handle directions, texts, lights and naps with just a little setup.
  • Industry observers note that it's 11PM and raining.
  • Industry observers note that the good news is you can still set one up before your next night out, and while you're at it, a few more are worth adding.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your Apple Watch can handle directions, texts, lights and naps with just a little setup.

Industry observers note that it's 11PM and raining. You're stuck outside a bar you'd never heard of until about six hours ago, trying to shout your home address into your wrist for the third time while someone else's Uber pulls up in front of you. Your Apple Watch could have had you on your way home with a single tap, if only you'd spent five minutes setting up a shortcut instead of doomscrolling.

Industry observers note that the good news is you can still set one up before your next night out, and while you're at it, a few more are worth adding. Your Watch can also text your better half an ETA as you leave work, switch off the lights you always leave on downstairs when you get into bed, put you down for a 20-minute nap without disturbing you and keep its screen dark while you're driving.

It has been revealed that shortcuts are made in the Shortcuts app on your iPhone, and they'll only appear on your wrist once you flip the Show on Apple Watch switch in each shortcut's settings. After you've set them up, you can run them from the Shortcuts app, a watch face complication or a Smart Stack widget (or the Action button if you've got an Ultra). If you've got an iPhone 15 Pro or newer, you can also describe what you want in plain English and let Apple Intelligence build a shortcut for you.

If you're out somewhere unfamiliar, after a night out or a long day at a conference, the last thing you want to be doing is dictating your full address into a tiny screen. Adding a Get Me Home shortcut helps you avoid all this.

In a recent development, open Shortcuts on your iPhone, tap the plus button and search for the Open Directions action. Tap the destination field, choose Location and pick your saved home address. You can also choose walking, driving or public transit directions and your preferred maps app. To name the shortcut, tap the title at the top of the screen and select Rename, then pick a house icon and a color. Finally, tap the info button, open Details and turn on Show on Apple Watch.

To add this to your watch face, touch and hold the face, tap Edit, swipe across to the complications screen, choose a slot, scroll to Shortcuts and pick the Get Me Home shortcut you just created. A circular slot on a face like Modular works particularly well here. If your route home usually involves a stop like a school pickup, Apple has you covered: iOS 26.4 added multi-stop driving directions to the same action.

Industry observers note that "What time will you be back?" is probably the most commonly sent text in any household. Most of the time your phone will ping with it just as you're walking to the car with your hands full. But you can set up a Watch shortcut that works out how long your journey home will take from wherever you are and sends that estimate to the people you choose.

It's quick to set up. Start a upcoming shortcut and search for Get Travel Time in the search bar at the bottom of the screen, then set the destination to your saved home address. Add a Text action and write something like "Leaving now, home in" followed by the Travel Time variable. Add the Send Message action the same way and choose who you'd like it to go to. Since iOS 27, recipients can include groups as well as individual people.

It has been revealed that you can make this a single-tap shortcut by switching on Show on Apple Watch and adding it as a complication or a Smart Stack widget. Run it once on your iPhone first, since it will ask permission to use your location and send messages. If you'd prefer not to tap anything, you can instead turn the shortcut into an automation that runs when you leave a saved location, like your workplace. In iOS 27, that trigger lives inside the shortcut and syncs across your other devices.

It has been revealed that you're finally home from the bar and your partner's already asleep, but you realize the downstairs lights are still on. Shouting "Hey Siri, turn off the lights!" in the middle of the night isn't exactly ideal, nor is trying to find the Home app on your Watch, which always takes longer than it should when you're pressed for time. A shortcut on your watch face does the job with one (silent) tap.

The easiest way to build this shortcut (if you've got an Apple Home setup) is to set up a scene in the Home app on your iPhone first. Give it a name like "Good Night," then set every light and outlet you want turned off. You can also add the things you want left on, like a hallway light at its lowest brightness or the thermostat at a cooler setting.

According to recent reports, next, create a new shortcut in Shortcuts and search the action list for Control Home. Choose the action that runs a scene, then pick Good Night. Turn on Show on Apple Watch and add it to your watch face as a complication like the others.

According to recent reports, the same approach works for the morning. A Good Morning scene, for example, could switch on the kitchen lights, turn the thermostat up and boil the kettle if you're British. You can put that shortcut next to Good Night on the same face, which makes it easy to switch between the two. You can also set up an automation on your iPhone that runs when you stop your alarm, which handles the morning half without a single tap.

Sources indicate that it's already easy enough to set a timer on your Watch, but setting everything up for a nap usually takes a few steps: start the timer, mute your notifications and then remember to unmute them when you wake up. If you don't mute your notifications, you can bet the group chat will come alive and buzz your wrist within 10 minutes. A simple dedicated nap shortcut can end all that.

Industry observers note that head to Shortcuts on your iPhone, search for the Start Timer action in the bottom search bar and set it to however long you like to nap. Twenty or 25 minutes is a sensible place to start. Then add Set Focus, choose Do Not Disturb and set it to turn off after the same amount of time, so your notifications come back on their own when the timer goes off. Name it Nap, give it a moon icon and switch on Show on Apple Watch.

According to recent reports, if you've got an Ultra, you can use the Action button instead. Go to Settings > Action Button on the Watch, choose Shortcut and pick Nap, then press the button to start the nap timer. Otherwise, you can put the shortcut on a complication or in the Smart Stack.

In a recent development, you can apply the same idea to your workouts. Your Watch knows when you start one, and a recent Shortcuts update added the Fitness app to the When I start a workout automation trigger. Pair that trigger with the same Do Not Disturb action and your phone stays silent during a run or gym session.

It's bad enough having modern LED headlights burn out your retinas while driving at night without your wrist also lighting up every time you turn the wheel. Thankfully, you can use Shortcuts to stop that from happening whenever your phone is connected to CarPlay.

In the Shortcuts app on your iPhone, create a new shortcut and add the Set Wake on Wrist Raise action, set to off. To also mute your Watch's sounds (you'll still feel haptic taps), add Set Theater Mode and set it to on. Theater Mode keeps the display dark until you tap it or press a button. Shortcuts may call it Cinema Mode, but it's the same thing.

In a recent development, you'll also need a trigger. Since iOS 27, automations live inside individual shortcuts rather than a separate tab, so add a CarPlay trigger, choose Connects and set it to run immediately so it won't ask for confirmation every time you get in the car. Next, duplicate the shortcut, switch Wake on Wrist Raise to on and Theater Mode to off, and set the trigger to Disconnects so your Watch goes back to normal when you park.

According to recent reports, the same pair of shortcuts will work with your car's regular Bluetooth connection or Driving Focus if you don't have CarPlay. Once your iPhone is talking to the car, you can add an intro to Apple CarPlay using Shortcuts, which runs from the same trigger.

In all, setting up the five shortcuts takes roughly 15 minutes, and each one saves you a few taps every day. The last one can also help cut down on driving distractions.

#2193. Nvidia Is Powering Brain-Computer Interfaces Now

Nvidia Is Powering Brain-Computer Interfaces Now

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (725 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A Michigan woman named Mary has a chip in her brain roughly the size of a dime.
  • In a recent development, made by brain-computer interface company Paradromics, the implant is outwardly invisible, but the speech decoding requires a cart full of electronics.
  • Today, Austin-based Paradromics declared a partnership with the AI chipmaker to use Nvidia’s hardware and software to process its brain data.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A Michigan woman named Mary has a chip in her brain roughly the size of a dime. Though she struggles to speak due to motor neuron disease, the implant allows her to express her thoughts through a synthesized voice on a computer.

In a recent development, made by brain-computer interface company Paradromics, the implant is outwardly invisible, but the speech decoding requires a cart full of electronics. A year from now, however, that cart will be transformed into a small box that can sit on her wheelchair, thanks to technology from Nvidia. Eventually, those electronics will be so small they’ll fit in a phone, notes Paradromics CEO and founder Matt Angle.

Today, Austin-based Paradromics declared a partnership with the AI chipmaker to use Nvidia’s hardware and software to process its brain data. Nvidia is facing a major leadership shakeup and federal scrutiny following longtime CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Sources indicate that though Mary has lost much of the use of her speaking muscles, neurons in her brain still fire when she attempts to speak. The Paradromics implant uses more than 400 embedded electrodes to capture those signals, and a computer uses artificial intelligence to make inferences about what she’s trying to say. The words appear on a screen, and the computer speaks the words for her.

That decoding process takes an incredible amount of computing power. The cart of electronics has to be plugged into an electrical outlet, and Mary must be within range of the cart in order to use her brain-computer interface.

Recent findings suggest that “We're producing a huge amount of data that has a lot of value, but we need to translate that neural data into applications in order to make this a really effective platform,” Angle notes. It’s why he calls brain-computer interfaces the ultimate case for edge computing, a distributed computing model that processes and stores data in physical devices close to where it is generated rather than sending it to a distant cloud or data center.

“We want to be able to do it through increasingly smaller and lower-power devices, and the people leading in that area are Nvidia,” he says.

It has been revealed that making brain-computer interfaces practical and portable for patients is a major challenge for the field. While these setups have become far more streamlined since their early days in academic labs, they still require lots of external electronics. Shrinking them down and reducing their power requirements would allow patients to be more mobile with these devices, using them wherever they go.

Paradromics plans to do that by using Nvidia’s Jetson, a low-powered computing module that will allow speech decoding to be done in a small device close to the user. It will also use Holoscan, Nvidia’s AI sensor processing software, to allow users to interact with computers and other devices with low lag time. Brain-computer interfaces will need to work alongside other sensors, such as cameras and microphones, and Holoscan will help process these different data streams together so applications can respond to both neural signals and the context around them.

Sources indicate that “Brain-computer interfaces must translate complex neural signals into meaningful actions in real time. Even small delays can make communication feel unnatural,” David Niewolny, Nvidia’s director of business development for health care and medical, tells WIRED via email. “Neural signals also change over time, requiring AI that can continuously adapt to the individual.” Nvidia’s technology processes neural signals and runs AI models in real time.

Reducing lag time is important for a brain-computer interface with a speech function so that customers can have naturally flowing conversation without delays.

Industry observers note that through the partnership, Paradromics will also be able to integrate Nvidia’s foundation models into its brain-computer interface. Vikash Gilja, chief scientific officer at Paradromics, notes AI models could help make synthesized voices more expressive and human-like. Also, if these models are running locally on Nvidia hardware, it means customers won’t have to be connected to the internet in order to use their devices.

Niewolny notes he sees “tremendous potential for AI to expand human capability.” Nvidia is working with other players in the brain-computer interface space, including Synchron. The chipmaker will not have access to brain data through these partnerships, he says.

CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler in $44 billion deal as AI supercharges cyberattacks

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (447 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • CrowdStrike plans to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in an all-stock deal that combines two significant security businesses at a time when artificial intelligence is supercharging attacks.
  • Shares of CrowdStrike dropped roughly 5% in early trading Monday, while Zscaler surged more than 20%.
  • The deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CrowdStrike plans to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in an all-stock deal that combines two significant security businesses at a time when artificial intelligence is supercharging attacks.

Shares of CrowdStrike dropped roughly 5% in early trading Monday, while Zscaler surged more than 20%.

The deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028. Under the agreement, Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each share.

CrowdStrike's acquisition pushes the Austin-based cyber vendor into the network security market and comes amid a massive year for cybersecurity dealmaking in the wake of high-profile hacks like Hugging Face.

According to recent reports, "With Zscaler, we're building cybersecurity's operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely," CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said in a statement. "We see a path to become the largest AI safety and security tech giant the world has ever seen.".

Recent outages affecting Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration and JPMorgan Chase have sparked anxiety as businesses accelerate software patching and upgrades to aging systems in an effort to prevent bad actors from exploiting software vulnerabilities with AI.

Industry observers note that crowdStrike has been a major beneficiary of skyrocketing demand for AI security, with shares soaring about 80% this year as of Monday's open. Zscaler shares are up about 5% year to date after Monday's surge. Their combined market value exceeded $265 billion as of Friday's close, behind market leader Palo Alto Networks at $282 billion.

The deal marks CrowdStrike's biggest acquisition to date and is among the largest in the sector as businesses consolidate and ramp up defenses to fend off AI-powered attacks.

Last year, Google revealed plans to acquire Wiz for $32 billion. In 2024 Cisco shelled about $28 billion for Splunk. Competitor Palo Alto Networks has also spent billions on several cyber and AI businesses, including startup Applied Compute and a $25 billion deal for CyberArk, which it closed earlier this year.

Analysts view the Zscaler deal as a major AI security opportunity, allowing CrowdStrike to capture more customer security spending and close a significant gap with Palo Alto.

"The addition of ZS to CRWD's platform could bring more breadth in an era of vendor consolidation and, more importantly, network security to position the company more effectively for rising demand for AI Sovereignty," wrote analysts at JPMorgan.

CrowdStrike on Monday also reported better-than-expected fiscal third-quarter results, including earnings of 34 cents per share on $1.58 billion in revenue. That topped the 31 cents per share on $1.53 billion in revenue forecast by LSEG.

Zscaler's fiscal first-quarter earnings, also released on Monday, likewise surpassed estimates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Enterprise customer experience firm Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, remarked on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles the company’s valuation to $30 billion. The new raise comes within six months of its previous round, which valued the company at $15 billion.

The fresh round was led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors who have led previous rounds, including Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV, and Tiger Global.

Sources indicate that enterprise automation is among the few areas where AI has seen rapid adoption. In a recent development, that said, Sierra is working along similar lines as other customer experience players in the market, which is creating a platform to build agents and partner with model developers to provide choices to enterprises. As personal and work agents interact with enterprise systems, Sierra is also working on creating protocol definitions for agents with companies like Meta, Stripe, and Walmart.

Sierra will use the fresh cash build to its technology stack to layer agents for servicing, and hire more sales folks to sign and maintain enterprise contracts faster than its rivals.

Tech Report: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, board chair

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia’s board of directors has voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman of the board, just 11 days after he resigned in the wake of multiple scandals.
  • It has been revealed that the reinstatement, declared Monday morning, is “effective immediately” and was based in part on “input from senior levels of the United States government” that assured the board members that “Mr.
  • In a recent development, that assurance comes despite Huang’s admitted affair with a woman who, US intelligence sources believe, was working as a Chinese spy and allegations that Nvidia had subverted export controls meant to keep Nvidia chips from reaching China.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia’s board of directors has voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman of the board, just 11 days after he resigned in the wake of multiple scandals.

It has been revealed that the reinstatement, declared Monday morning, is “effective immediately” and was based in part on “input from senior levels of the United States government” that assured the board members that “Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”.

In a recent development, that assurance comes despite Huang’s admitted affair with a woman who, US intelligence sources believe, was working as a Chinese spy and allegations that Nvidia had subverted export controls meant to keep Nvidia chips from reaching China. It also comes despite multiple developing investigations from multiple different government departments into those and other alleged national security, accounting, and corporate governance failures.

Huang had been seeking a return to Nvidia since shortly after his resignation, reportedly forming a war room to strategize how best to bring it to pass. Last week, Huang posted on social media that “if the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the firm, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”.

President Trump has also been a major backer of Huang’s return to Nvidia. “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang,” he wrote on Truth Social last week. “It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.” In a social media post immediately following the reinstatement, Trump called it “the correct and proper decision” and confirmed that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.”.

Appearing on CNBC Monday morning, Trump said that he had spoken to the Nvidia board “directly and indirectly” about Huang’s reinstatement, and that Huang “did nothing wrong.” Losing “the brainpower of someone like [Huang]” would be “a much bigger threat” than anything related to his alleged interactions with China, Trump said.

“We’ve done a very thorough investigation and the investigation showed that… he had bad judgement having to do with somewhat unrelated incidents,” Trump said. “You have to protect our geniuses and there aren’t enough of them.”.

In a recent development, huang’s tenure at Nvidia dates back to the company’s founding in 1993, when he and three cofounders were focused on the then-nascent field of GPU hardware aimed at PC gamers. In the decades since, the highly parallel cores in those GPUs have been embraced first by cryptocurrency miners and then AI companies, propelling the company to its position as the most valuable in the world at its October peak.

Nvidia stock—the price of which had sunk roughly 25 percent since Huang’s resignation was confirmed and nearly 50 percent since its peak—was up about 30 percent in early morning trading in the immediate aftermath of Huang’s reinstatement announcement.

Huang’s return in some ways echoes that of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who was fired almost exactly three years ago after the board stated it “no longer has confidence in his ability to continue leading OpenAI.” Two weeks later, Altman was back at the helm after many employees threatened a mass revolt and departure if he wasn’t brought back.

In Huang’s case, the revolt following his departure came not from employees but from fellow titans of the tech industry. Executives including Altman, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, xAI’s Elon Musk and Anduril’s Palmer Luckey are among the prominent industry figures who have publicly offered him support in the days since his resignation.

In its statement, the Nvidia board reiterated that it has retained independent counsel and formed a committee of independent directors to investigate what it calls Huang’s targeting by “a foreign intelligence effort.” The company has also formed a National Security and Export Control Committee to “oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” and is seeking to hire a upcoming chief compliance officer position.

This story has been updated to reflect Trump’s statements to CNBC.

NVIDIA reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and president, effective immediately

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • So much for the board not intending to bring him back.
  • NVIDIA has reversed course and reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO and president, effective immediately.
  • Recent findings suggest that "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a latest industrial revolution," Huang noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So much for the board not intending to bring him back.

NVIDIA has reversed course and reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO and president, effective immediately. The board stated in a statement it held a series of meetings and discussions with Huang, who resigned 11 days ago following reports of multiple affairs. It added that it had "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and determined that reinstating Huang posed no risk to national security.

Recent findings suggest that "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a latest industrial revolution," Huang noted. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work.".

It has been revealed that NVIDIA said the board members voted unanimously to reappoint Huang, just a few days after Jones said on an earnings call that they did "not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." In his first public statement since stepping down on November 12, Huang said last week he "would be honored" to return to the helm of the manufacturer he cofounded. He said he'd "seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners and customers" for him step back into the CEO position.

In a recent development, huang's reinstatement follows two weeks of turmoil at NVIDIA. The board stated on November 8 it had opened an investigation into reports that Huang was "the target of a foreign intelligence effort." He admitted to having an affair following reports linking him to Alice Huang, a tech executive suspected of being a Chinese spy. On November 11, The Latest York Times reported Huang also had an affair with one of his subordinates at NVIDIA. By the following morning, he had departed the company. The board appointed Jones as board chair and Kress — NVIDIA's Chief Financial Officer and Executive Vice President — as interim CEO.

The board met on Sunday night to vote on Huang's reinstatement, according to Semafor, which previously reported that several directors had pushed for him to return. President Donald Trump was among the external figures who called for Huang to be reappointed. Trump welcomed the board's decision.

"The country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the success and prosperity of not only the company, but the American economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to national security," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the company's compliance with US export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and patriotic duty to protect US national security.".

It has been revealed that semafor reported that Trump actually called into NVIDIA's board meeting. "President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses," White House communications director Steven Cheung told the publication.

Trump's latest financial disclosure indicated that, in September, he bought up to $265,000 worth of NVIDIA stock and sold up to $15,000 worth of his shares in the manufacturer. The White House told Reuters that third-party financial institutions manage Trump's portfolio. NVIDIA's share price skyrocketed by around 33 percent after Huang's reinstatement.

NVIDIA's board "believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Jones mentioned in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the firm. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA's Chief Financial Officer.".

According to recent reports, NVIDIA's investigation is ongoing and Huang noted he'll fully cooperate. He's also set to testify before Congress on December 1. Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the House Intelligence Committee. NVIDIA General Counsel Tim Teter will do the same the following day. It appears they'll testify behind closed doors, though their remarks will at least be transcribed.

Meanwhile, Alice Huang is reportedly under federal investigation over her alleged ties to Chinese companies that are mentioned to have smuggled in chips from the likes of NVIDIA and Super Micro Computer in the face of US export restrictions. In 2023, she became a director of Singaporean cloud computing tech giant Megaspeed, which is said to have since bought over $4 billion worth of NVIDIA chips and equipment. NVIDIA placed Megaspeed on its "no sell" list in 2025. Megaspeed said Alice Huang left the company two months later. The US Commerce and Justice departments said last week they'd been investigating Megaspeed over potential export control violations since 2024.

Industry observers note that last week, NVIDIA set up a committee to ensure the company's compliance with US export controls. It said on Monday it was recruiting a Chief Compliance Officer as well. NVIDIA added that it will "continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.".

Upgrade, November 23, 2026, 11:14AM ET: Added details about Trump's NVIDIA holdings and the company's increased share price.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that bluetooth headphones and earbuds are now incredibly common, and more people than ever own a pair. But despite how long Bluetooth has been around, pairing Bluetooth headphones to a computer can still be fiddly. Microsoft hasn't helped, either, with Windows 11's Bluetooth stability a constant bugbear, too, making things even worse — but more on that later.

On paper, connecting headphones to a Windows 11 computer is relatively straightforward. The simplest way is to click the speaker icon in the bottom-right of the taskbar to open the quick settings panel, click the arrow next to the Bluetooth icon, and make sure the Bluetooth toggle is set to the on position.

Industry observers note that then, put your device in pairing mode. How you enter pairing mode differs between products, so refer to the documentation for your specific headphones or earbuds. You'll usually need to hold down a button, often with the Bluetooth logo. Select your device when it appears in the list of Bluetooth devices, and you're connected.

Sources indicate that connecting your Bluetooth earbuds or headphones to a Windows 11 PC is simple when things work correctly, but that doesn't always happen. Bluetooth performance has long been a weak point on Windows 11, and Microsoft was still trying to improve things as of September 2026. If things don't work, you're probably not doing anything wrong and should look into other solutions, like updating your wireless drivers or rebooting your PC.

You can also pair Bluetooth headphones by pressing Win + I to open Windows 11's Settings and selecting Bluetooth & devices from the left-hand menu. Make sure that Bluetooth is on, as indicated by the toggle. Below that toggle, you'll see the name your PC shows up as on other devices, which only matters if the device you're pairing has a screen. If you're pairing for the first time, click Add device, then click Bluetooth. Make sure your headphones are in pairing mode. The PC will begin to scan for ready-to-pair Bluetooth devices. Once your device appears in the Windows dialog, click it, and it should pair after a few moments.

According to recent reports, some Bluetooth accessories support Swift Pair, which tries to proactively pair devices. Popular headphones, including the Sony WH-1000XM6 and Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro — and previous models from those product lines — come with the feature. To set up a device with Swift Pair, make sure Bluetooth is enabled on your PC, then turn the device on and put it into pairing mode. You should see a pop-up on the PC asking if you want to connect with that device. Click Connect. Devices connected via Swift Pair will automatically connect to your PC.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Monday, President Trump praised Nvidia’s decision on Monday to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as the tech giant’s CEO and president, saying on his social network Truth Social that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.”.

Industry observers note that the Nvidia board’s statement had also referred to consultations with “senior levels of the United States government” as informing its decision. It mentioned that, based on that input, Mr. Huang’s reinstatement was deemed not a national security risk.

In his comments on Monday, Trump claimed that U.S. Attorney General [Todd Blanche] had found no evidence that Mr. Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. It’s an unusual statement for a U.S. president to make, as the Attorney General typically conducts those investigations independently. Notably, Attorney General Blanche has not yet made a formal statement on the case.

Industry observers note that there’s also indication that President Trump may have been aware of the decision before the announcement by the Nvidia board. Speaking to a PBS journalist over the weekend, he remarked of Huang “he’s back where he should be and we see he did absolutely nothing wrong.” Asked to clarify about whether he meant Huang would be reinstated, Trump said, “I hope so, I hope so.”.

Huang was accused of having multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a direct report at Nvidia and another unnamed employee. However, the affair of most concern was the one with the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation). Ms. Huang was an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed, which had purchased billions in Nvidia chips over the past couple of years. This relationship had raised national security concerns about whether the CEO ties to Ms. Huang could have compromised sensitive information or facilitated China’s access to advanced U.S. AI chips, which are subject to export restrictions.

Sources indicate that trump stated last week that he believed this relationship didn’t threaten the U.S.’s national security, and instead said that no one had proven she’s a spy. “She may not be a spy,” the president said, adding that “China plays games with us, and we play games with China.”.

Trump’s full statement on Huang’s return, released on Monday, is below.

The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security. Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rumors have been swirling for days that we’d be getting a final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday, the penultimate film in the MCU’s Phase Six, heralding the end of the so-called “Multiverse Saga.” The rumors were true: Marvel just released the trailer, featuring pretty much every superhero ever represented in the MCU. And it looks like the Avengers will face consequences for messing with the timeline to reverse the blip in End Game.

As previously reported, the film takes place 14 months after the events of Thunderbolts*. Per the official logline: “Beloved heroes from three distinct universes will be set on a deadly collision course and face an existential threat unlike anything they’ve ever encountered.” Those universes are Earth-616 (the Avengers, Wakandans, and Upcoming Avengers), Earth-828 (Fantastic Four), and the “original” X-Men.

In a recent development, cast-wise, we have Avengers favorites Thor (Chris Hemsworth), the new Captain America (Anthony Mackie), Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Ant-Man (Paul Rudd), Falcon (Danny Ramirez), and Loki (Tom Hiddleston). Then there’s the Wakandan contingent: Shuri as the new Black Panther (Letitia Wright), M’Baku (Winston Duke), and Namor (Tenoch Huerta Mejia), as well as Alex Livinalli as Namor’s ally, Attuma. And, of course, Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom.

We also have the Thunderbolts* (aka Latest Avengers): John Walker/US Agent (Wyatt Russell), Yelena Belova (Florence Pugh), Bob/Sentry (Lewis Pullman), Red Guardian (David Harbour), and Ghost (Hannah John-Kamen). And the Fantastic Four: Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal), Sue Storm (Vanessa Kirby), Ben Grimm (Ebon Moss-Bachrach), and Johnny Storm (Joseph Quinn). We’ll also see Charles Xavier (Patrick Stewart), Beast (Kelsey Grammer), Magneto (Ian McKellen), Mystique (Rebecca Romijn), Nightcrawler (Alan Cumming), and Cyclops (James Marsden).

For good measure, Marvel threw in Gambit (Channing Tatum) and Xu Shang-Chi (Simu Liu). There will be plenty of cameos, like Steve Rogers (Chris Evans), revealed in one of four sneak teasers last year. We can also expect to see (at least briefly) Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell), Spider-Man (Tom Holland), Hawkeye (Jeremy Renner), Doctor Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch), Thor’s adopted daughter, Love (India Rose Hemsworth), and Scott Lang’s daughter, Cassie (Kathryn Newton).

The first trailer dropped in July, just before San Diego Comic-Con, and really just consisted of a heck of a lot of cameos, as the superheroes from the three universes met each other over an ominous voiceover by Thor, warning of an unprecedented threat. It ended with the return of Steve Rogers—and guess what, he’s still worthy of Thor’s hammer, Mjölnir. The following month, Marvel dropped another trailer during its D23 fan event, hinting at Doctor Doom’s tragic backstory.

According to recent reports, rogers features prominently in the fresh trailer, which opens with him and Peggy discussing how they made the right choice, but Steve still feels bad about hiding this truth from their son, who is now a young teen. We knew he had opted to stay in the past and build a life with Peggy at the end of End Game; what we didn’t know is that they did this in the same alternate universe as the Fantastic Four, who show up to recruit him to the latest cause.

It has been revealed that “Years ago, we did what was needed to make the world right,” Rogers continues in a voiceover. “But we didn’t know those choices would have consequences.” Whatever the roots of Doom’s grudge against the Avengers, he believes “all of you have lived stolen lives,” adding an ominous: “But now you must give them back.”.

It has been revealed that the rest is largely footage we’ve seen before, with Thor admitting, “I don’t even know who half of you are” to the assembled superheroes, before making his call for them to “stand together” against Doom. Among the new footage is Marsden’s Cyclops facing off against Doom and several Sentinels: He calls, “To me, my X-Men,” except it’s everyone who responds. We also see Steve and Thor bantering about how Steve wielding Mjölnir bothers the Norse god more than he cares to admit. There’s no sign of Wanda Maximoff/The Scarlet Witch, whom Doom revived in a post-credits scene at the end of VisionQuest. She might be among the trio of Latverian witches that briefly appear in the trailer.

Verdict: We don’t know if Doomsday will measure up to Infinity War and End Game, but it’s bound to provide a spectacle.

Industry observers note that avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18, 2026. It will battle it out against Dune: Part III, which also drops that same day. Avengers: Secret Wars is at the moment slated for release on December 17, 2027, and will mark the conclusion of the MCU’s Phase Six.

#2180. What is Sound Glow on HomePods, and how do you get it on your Apple speaker?

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (678 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

What is Sound Glow on HomePods, and how do you get it on your Apple speaker?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (678 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple’s latest HomePod update makes the top of your speaker glow in sync with music.
  • Apple's HomePod has a basic set of lights on top that don't do much beyond glowing when Siri is listening or when something is playing.
  • HomePods don't have a traditional display like Apple's HomeView.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s latest HomePod update makes the top of your speaker glow in sync with music.

Apple's HomePod has a basic set of lights on top that don't do much beyond glowing when Siri is listening or when something is playing. But following the launch of the HomePod mini 2, Apple also introduced a upcoming feature called Sound Glow that makes better use of these lights. When turned on, the top of the speaker becomes a colorful light show synced to the song you're listening to — and the good news is that it's not exclusive to the latest HomePod mini. The feature is part of HomePod Software 27.2 and also works with the original HomePod mini and the HomePod 2 (the larger model). Here's a breakdown of how Sound Glow works and how you can enable (or disable) it on your HomePods.

HomePods don't have a traditional display like Apple's HomeView. Instead, Apple has included an array of LEDs on top along with a touch-sensitive surface that lets owners access quick controls such as volume and play/pause. With the latest HomePod software update, these LEDs are now used to make HomePods a little more fun with Sound Glow. Now, when you play a song, the speaker pulls colors from the album art and pulses them in time with the music's beat. Listening to Taylor Swift's The Life of a Showgirl will result in predominantly green and orange lights, while Miley Cyrus's Endless Summer Vacation will make the lights on your HomePod turn blue.

Recent findings suggest that apple indicates that the light animation reacts in real time to the bass and treble of the song being played, so two songs from the same album will glow differently. Also, Sound Glow isn't limited to songs — it also works with podcasts and Apple's ambient sounds. For instance, the Rain soundscape features an animation with a gentle pitter-patter effect. Songs without artwork or videos revert to the HomePod's standard white light. It all happens automatically and you really don't have to think about it.

It has been revealed that there are a few limitations worth noting, though. Don't expect Sound Glow to fully light up your living room — the lights aren't bright enough to do that unless the room is completely dark. The feature is also not available on the original HomePod released in 2018, even though it can be updated to the latest HomePod software. You'll also need an Apple Intelligence-enabled device paired with your HomePods for Sound Glow to work — that means an iPhone 15 Pro or newer, an M1 Mac or newer or one of the latest iPads. An Apple TV running tvOS 27 also does the trick to enable Sound Glow on your HomePods.

In a recent development, if you have HomePods and a compatible Apple device, setting up Sound Glow is easy, but you'll need to make sure they're all running the latest software first. That means HomePod Software 27.2 or later on your HomePods and iOS 27.2 on your iPhone or iPad. HomePods usually patch automatically after a while, but you can confirm in the Home app from another Apple device. Tap the three-dot button and select Home Settings, then look for the Software Update menu. Even a brand-upcoming HomePod mini 2 may need a software update, since it may ship with a version prior to 27.2 installed.

Once everything is up to date, you can finally enable Sound Glow. Go back to the Home app's main screen and tap your HomePod, then go to Settings and scroll down until you find the Sound Glow toggle. Just flip it on, and the feature will work — you'll need to do this for each HomePod individually. Ask Siri to play a song or use AirPlay on your iPhone to try out Sound Glow and see if it's working. And if you don't like Sound Glow, turning it off requires pretty much the same steps as turning it on, but now you'll have to flip the toggle to off instead.

The Dutch Data Protection Authority is urging consumers not to buy AI-enabled camera glasses, warning that they compromise the privacy of nearby bystanders and risk the safety of their people.

The authority, whose recent statement falls just short of an outright ban, stated that use of the internet-enabled and always-on glasses to record people in public is “almost always prohibited.”.

Sources indicate that critics have dubbed these smart wearables as “pervert glasses” for their propensity to be used to video people without their permission, particularly to harass women. While some glasses have warning lights when customers are recording, privacy advocates have argued that these alerts are not clear enough. Some people have even made phone apps capable of detecting nearby smart glasses wearers.

It has been revealed that the Dutch data protection authority warned that the glasses also produce wrong results and unsafe results. In one test carried out by the Dutch authority, a pair of unnamed glasses “gave dating advice to an adult who indicated that they are interested in a minor.” The glasses also incorrectly read a medicine label and claimed to have called an ambulance when it had not.

The Dutch government’s advice follows a similar move by the Norwegian government, which in September remarked it was considering a ban on camera-enabled devices.

Oregon and Virginia said the company broke state consumer protection laws.

The attorneys general of Oregon and Virginia have filed lawsuits against SpaceX Super Intelligence, accusing Elon Musk's conglomerate firm of violating state consumer protection laws by allowing users of its Grok AI chatbot to create non-consensual sexually explicit content. The lawsuit alleged that SpaceXSI released Grok's "spicy mode" as a way to "push its lagging product to tens of millions of latest users," which allowed for the creation of child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

Industry observers note that "This lawsuit is about seeking justice for the millions of Virginians who maintain accounts on X and were misled by the firm's false reassurances that their data and images would be safe on the platform," Jay Jones, Virginia's attorney general, remarked in a press release. "When xAI allowed Grok's creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it.".

This morning, X Safety posted that people using Grok for sexually explicit deepfakes "deliberately" violated the Terms of Service, adding that it will "keep testing and adjusting those protections as these abusers change tactics." X Safety also said that "protecting children is non-negotiable" and that CSAM "has no place on X or in Grok, and neither do explicit images of real people made without their consent.".

X Safety's post also said that the company would "take appropriate measures, including actioning accounts and notifying law enforcement," when users circumvent Grok's safeguards to create this type of content. Earlier this year, SpaceXSI filed a lawsuit against one of its users for creating sexual images of real people without their consent.

Sources indicate that beyond Oregon and Virginia, SpaceXSI faced several regulatory investigations and lawsuits in response to people generating illegal content. The City of Baltimore pursued legal action against Musk's manufacturer, claiming that Grok broke the city's Consumer Protection Ordinance; the UK's media authority and the California attorney general launched separate investigations into xAI and Grok.

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jensen Huang is stepping back into his role as chief executive of Nvidia effective immediately.
  • The stunning reversal comes 11 days after Huang resigned as CEO from the firm he cofounded 33 years ago, and after multiple declarations from the board of directors that it had no intention of reinstating him.
  • “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers,” said recently appointed board chair Harvey Jones in a press release announcing the decision.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jensen Huang is stepping back into his role as chief executive of Nvidia effective immediately.

The stunning reversal comes 11 days after Huang resigned as CEO from the firm he cofounded 33 years ago, and after multiple declarations from the board of directors that it had no intention of reinstating him. On Monday, they took a conciliatory tone.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers,” said recently appointed board chair Harvey Jones in a press release announcing the decision.

Recent findings suggest that in that announcement the board noted it was “satisfied with respect to Mr Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia,” and that it had “received input from senior levels of the United States government” on the way to its decision. On Monday morning, President Donald Trump posted that the Nvidia board “has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO.”.

“I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” stated Huang in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”.

Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on November 12, and longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress was installed as his interim replacement. Five days later, Huang publicly announced that he was open to resuming his role as chief executive, noting the “outpouring of calls” from “employees, investors, business partners, and customers” advocating for his return.

“If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang wrote.

The day Huang resigned, many Nvidia employees spoke up in his support. As reported by WIRED, employees left more than 1,600 comments on an internal “suggestion box” post in which they urged the company’s board to reinstall him as CEO.

It has been revealed that in the days following, a public petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement began circulating. At the time of writing, it has amassed more than 200,000 online signatures, the majority of whom self-identified as Nvidia shareholders. Tech elites like Elon Musk and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan have claimed that they were going to sign the petition or had signed it.

Huang’s reinstatement marks a total reversal from the public stance of Nvidia’s board of directors, which stated during the tech giant’s November 17 earnings call that it “does not intend” to reinstate him as CEO. WIRED has further reported that the board was alarmed by what one source described as Huang’s “lying” over the last year or so.

In a recent development, president Donald Trump, who developed a close working relationship with Huang during his second administration, had indicated openness to Huang returning as CEO. Trump told reporters on November 16 that he “would not mind” if Huang returned as chief executive, adding that he believed he had “learned a big lesson.”.

Huang’s resignation followed days of scrutiny over several extramarital romantic relationships: one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who has no known relation to Jensen, one with a Nvidia employee who directly reported to Huang, and one with a different Nvidia employee.

Huang’s relationship with Alice became the subject of particularly intense focus on November 6, when The Fresh York Times and Financial Times reported that US intelligence officials suspected that Alice may be an asset of the Chinese Ministry of State Security, both citing an intelligence briefing that circulated among top Trump administration officials last year. In the days since, some reports and Trump administration officials have questioned the accuracy of that intelligence. The Chinese government has consistently rejected claims that Alice was one of its spies.

According to recent reports, alice was the chief executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI company that’s been accused of helping Chinese tech companies use Nvidia’s most advanced chips at overseas locations, effectively sidestepping US export restrictions. Alice has also reportedly worked as a television reporter, at HSBC’s Hong Kong-based private banking arm, and at an investment bank backed by the Chinese state.

Sources indicate that huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, purportedly with the mission of bringing realistic 3D graphics to personal computers. For many years, the manufacturer was primarily known within the gaming community. It didn’t become a household name until the recent AI boom, when its graphic processing units (GPUs) became a crucial piece of infrastructure for powering advanced AI models.

Nvidia controlled about 90 percent of the global GPU market as of September 2026. The year prior, it became the first ever company to be valued at more than $4 trillion, though its stock price has been in precipitous decline since Huang’s resignation.

Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike has agreed to buy Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal, the companies confirmed Monday.

Crowdstrike and Zscaler said that the deal will create the “largest single addressable market” for cybersecurity, which will enable the companies to better position themselves for the AI era.

Zscaler is a San Jose, Calif.-based tech company that provides cloud cybersecurity products to about 8,000 enterprise companies. The company offers zero-trust technology, a security feature that requires employees to authenticate each and every time they access an internal system or resource. The aim is to protect against hackers from stealing credentials and using them to gain unfettered access to a company’s network.

Sources indicate that crowdStrike, which secures the computers, laptops, phones and other devices connected to a firm’s network, stated the deal will unite its endpoint protection software with Zscaler’s zero-trust platform to better defend their customers against data breaches. By combining the two products, CrowdStrike and Zscaler say that they can offer “superior protection” to their customers.

In remarks on Monday, the companies said that the acquisition will help customers safely adopt AI.

The deal, which is subject to regulatory approval, is expected to close around this time next year.

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (692 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

What the green flashing light on your Roku remote is telling you

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (692 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A remote that won't cooperate can put your streaming plans on hold.
  • Regardless of what you think of Fox's takeover, Roku is still an undeniable force in smart TVs.
  • Recent findings suggest that one of the reasons for the platform's popularity is its simplicity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A remote that won't cooperate can put your streaming plans on hold. Here's how to work out what's wrong and get back to the content you love.

Regardless of what you think of Fox's takeover, Roku is still an undeniable force in smart TVs. The manufacturer's products are an easy choice when looking for the best streaming devices, and of course a number of TVs now ship with Roku OS built in, most notably models from TCL and Hisense. Roku is the main game in town for brands that are not using Google TV, Fire TV or their own proprietary software.

Recent findings suggest that one of the reasons for the platform's popularity is its simplicity. That noted, there are times when the platform can be a little obtuse, mysterious blinking lights on the remote being a prime example. It's easy to assume that means a problem — but what, exactly?

Recent findings suggest that if you're dealing with a flashing green LED on your Roku remote, the fix could be very straightforward, simply requiring fresh batteries or a recharge, depending on the model. In some circumstances, however, you may need to do more or replace your remote entirely. Hopefully you've already got the Roku app on your phone as a backup, which can save you in a pinch when your remote is on the fritz.

As we just suggested, one reason for the light may be that your remote's batteries are low. If that's the case, swapping in fresh batteries (if there's no built-in one) should rapidly solve the problem. If you find this is happening too frequently, though, it may be because you're using rechargeable batteries. Alkalines are costlier in the long run — but Roku does recommend them for remotes with replaceable batteries. You can check battery levels in advance by navigating to Settings > Remotes & devices > Remotes > Your remote > About.

It has been revealed that you'll also see this light if you're trying to set up a replacement remote. Using your old one or the Roku app, you may need to head to Settings > Remotes & devices > Add devices > Remote > Continue to complete the process. You'll definitely see green flashing if you trigger a remote's physical pairing controls, which is done by holding a dedicated button or the Back and Home buttons simultaneously for five seconds.

Recent findings suggest that there's no need to be worried unless the light is flashing rapidly after re-pairing. If that's going on, it's a sign that your remote is probably broken and needs to be replaced. Note that you can also buy third-party remotes; sticking with one of Roku's official options should get you better support and features. Whatever you choose, verify that it's going to be compatible with your particular TV or streamer.

Industry observers note that if you've run through all of the above steps short of replacing your remote, one remaining option is to restart it. If it uses replaceable batteries, take them out, then press any two buttons before reinserting the batteries, negative sides first. If it uses a built-in battery, hold down its physical pairing controls (see the last section) for 20 seconds.

At this point, there's not much else you can try short of clearing the cache on your Roku or updating or rebooting your Roku device, or you could learn how to reset your Roku. Be warned that if you try a reset, you'll have to reconfigure everything as if it were right out of the box. It's also unlikely to solve a green light problem, since as we've established, that's normally related to battery levels or pairing, not buggy software.

If worst comes to worst, you may be stuck using your phone for control. The pros and cons of sharing your location

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (739 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some apps really do need to know where you are, but plenty of others don't.
  • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
  • Industry observers note that when you download an app on a smartphone, you're usually prompted to agree to a list of permissions it needs to function.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some apps really do need to know where you are, but plenty of others don't.

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Industry observers note that when you download an app on a smartphone, you're usually prompted to agree to a list of permissions it needs to function. You may be asked to share your device's location when the app is open or grant unrestricted access in the background. Even website pop-ups halt your scrolling to ask for your location.

Industry observers note that it can be difficult to pick between staying in the dark and trading your location for services like maps, food deliveries and device tracking. Outside of those use cases, you may want to share your location from your iPhone with a friend or family member.

It has been revealed that today's devices have more safety features than they used to. Google, for instance, reviews Android apps that ask for background location access. But location data can be resold to third parties, so sharing it with apps and services you don't trust is risky. Here's how to weigh the pros and cons.

It has been revealed that staying connected makes your devices easier to find. While Find My is an easy smartphone anti-theft pick, sharing your location data with Apple AirTags and Tile trackers that work via Bluetooth lets you see your belongings in real time on a map. They can even play audio alerts, so you won't have to worry about losing your car keys inside your apartment again.

On a night out, people often share their location with friends for a sense of safety. Uber's Share My Trip feature lets you send your trip status and live location to up to five contacts. Snapchat's Snap Map, meanwhile, uses your location to track where you've made memories and find hotspots of activity to plan your next hangout. If you've set up the Personal Safety app on your Pixel phone, it can automatically call 911 and share your location if it detects a severe car crash.

According to recent reports, you can also share your location for a set time on your iPhone. iOS 26 lets you share for an hour, a day or indefinitely, and iOS 27 adds a custom option that runs from 15 minutes to 30 days. iOS 27 also lets you temporarily hide your location from people you normally share it with. On Android smartphones, Google's Find My Device app lets contacts share their location with you for a set duration as well. If you're meeting someone, you can also share your real-time location in Google Maps with an estimated time of arrival.

Sources indicate that sometimes you have no choice but to share your location data. Getting directions from Google Maps or Apple Maps, whether in a new city or on your home turf, requires letting the app see where you are. As a parent, you may want to see your children's location via services like Google Family Link. As a partner, maybe you shouldn't, even though many couples do. A Life360 survey of 1,000 US adults in relationships found that 95 percent use some form of location-sharing tech.

This can take a turn for the worse when personal safety is involved. Fitness-tracking apps like Strava store information on your jogging routines, revealing patterns that a stalker may use to deliberately run into you if you leave your information public. This goes for geotagged social media posts as well. Adding your location to a public Instagram Story might help your friends find you, but live updates like these may also draw attention from strangers.

In some cases, you may be able to get away with giving your location data momentarily or refusing altogether. Try not to hand out your location data to services that don't really need it to function. Delivery apps work just fine with manually entered addresses instead of being allowed to track your location. You can also use their browser-based versions to reduce the information you share.

Sources indicate that in 2022, Canadian privacy regulators found that Tim Horton's mobile app logged far more personal information than it had sought consent for, including detailed location data. As long as you're mindful of where your location data is being shared, you should be able to rely on the benefits of sharing while minimizing the odds of it falling into the wrong hands.

#2168. An unseen planet past Neptune may be in Earths weight class

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1088 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

An unseen planet past Neptune may be in Earths weight class

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1088 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Math points to our solar system having another planet in Earth's weight class far beyond Neptune, tugging distant icy bodies onto strange orbits, a new study proposes.
  • Industry observers note that that would make it far smaller than Planet Nine, a hypothesized giant world five to 10 times Earth's mass that has drawn most of the attention in the hunt for an undiscovered planet.
  • "Imagine discovering, after decades of mapping our solar system, that another planet has been hiding from us all this time," said lead researcher Patryk Sofia Lykawka, of Kindai University in Japan, in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Math points to our solar system having another planet in Earth's weight class far beyond Neptune, tugging distant icy bodies onto strange orbits, a new study proposes.

Industry observers note that that would make it far smaller than Planet Nine, a hypothesized giant world five to 10 times Earth's mass that has drawn most of the attention in the hunt for an undiscovered planet. No one has spotted this suspected world, nicknamed Planet X2, but these researchers argue it would explain the strangest orbits in the outer solar system better.

"Imagine discovering, after decades of mapping our solar system, that another planet has been hiding from us all this time," said lead researcher Patryk Sofia Lykawka, of Kindai University in Japan, in a statement.

Every search for a missing planet has started the same way, with something in space that doesn't add up. In the 1800s, astronomers noticed Uranus wasn't staying on its predicted path, and the culprit turned out to be Neptune. Percival Lowell thought Uranus was still misbehaving and went looking for a "Planet X," a search that led to Pluto in 1930. But Pluto proved far too small to explain the trouble. Today, clues come from farther out, in a growing collection of frozen worlds beyond Neptune that move in ways the known planets can't explain. To many astronomers, that hints that something is still out there — maybe one planet, maybe more.

Beyond Neptune, a vast spill of icy leftovers from the solar system's birth circles the sun. Most of these objects travel in the Kuiper Belt, a broad band 38 to 50 times as far from the sun as Earth. Over the past 20 years, astronomers have found more and more of these objects on steeply tilted or stretched-out orbits.

In a recent development, in the new study, the researchers built a computer model of the young solar system. It included the four giant planets, thousands of small icy bodies, and 1,500 Pluto-size worlds. Then, the computer worked out how each body tugged on the others, step by step, across 4.5 billion years. When the team added Planet X2, up to twice Earth's mass, its gravity pulled some icy objects out of Neptune's reach and tipped others onto steep angles. Together, those effects reproduced the orbits of every known oddball, including Sedna, a distant world that swings far beyond the planets on a long, narrow loop. Models without the planet fell far short, according to the paper, published in the journal Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.

Sources indicate that every hidden-planet study relies on computer models, but this one seems to replay more of the solar system's history. Early on, Neptune slowly drifted outward from the sun. As it moved, its gravity flung some icy objects far out and trapped others in orbits that march in step with Neptune.

Lykawka's own 2023 model skipped that drift and didn't include the main Kuiper Belt, where most known icy objects travel. It highlighted that Planet X2 could create the odd distant orbits, but not whether the planet would also wreck the parts of the belt that Neptune built. In the new model, Planet X2 creates the strange distant orbits and leaves the rest of the belt much like what astronomers see today.

A competing idea — that a few extra Mars- to Earth-size worlds formed among the giant planets and got flung around early on — fared worse in the team's model. The giant planets would have thrown those worlds out of the solar system within tens of millions of years — too fast to explain the strange orbits seen today.

Planet Nine faces problems of its own. Its backers proposed it after noticing that the orbits of a few distant icy objects seemed to point in roughly the same direction, as if something big had herded them into line. Other researchers have argued that the pattern may be a fluke, caused by having too few known objects and by telescopes watching only certain patches of sky. Several recently discovered distant objects follow orbits that don't fit what Planet Nine predicts, the authors say.

Sources indicate that in the researchers' best-fitting models, Planet X2 circles the sun at an average distance of about 33 billion to 46 billion miles. That's roughly 12 to 17 times as far out as Neptune, and nine to 13 times as far as Pluto. Even at its closest, the planet would stay nearly 19 billion miles from the sun — more than six times Neptune's distance. Its orbit would likely tilt only slightly from the path the other planets follow.

"If this planet exists, it could change how we understand the history of our solar system and how its most distant objects came to follow such unusual orbits," Lykawka remarked.

According to recent reports, the researchers admit the model doesn't fix everything. For example, compared with what a major sky survey found, the simulations predicted too few objects in the larger orbits the team studied.

The Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which photographs the night sky again and again, could settle the debate, catching the planet as a faint, slowly moving dot. That's a tall order for something so far from the sun's light. Another possibility is that Rubin could find enough distant icy objects to show whether their orbits carry Planet X2's gravitational fingerprints.

"We now have an opportunity to put this idea to the test," noted study co-author Jonti Horner, a professor at the University of Southern Queensland, in a statement. "As the Rubin Observatory surveys the sky, we will find fresh clues that help us understand the distant reaches of the Solar System — and whether another planet is still waiting to be discovered.".

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (952 w)
